 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Anand Kumar, Advocate
For the State : Mr. Dhurjati Kumar Prasad, GP-14
For NHAI : Mr. Iti Suman, Advocate
Learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the National Highway Authority of India and learned Counsel for the State are present.

2. The present writ petition has been filed for the following relief/s :-
"i) For issuance of an appropriate writ in the nature of Mandamus for commanding and directing the respondent authorities to make payment of compensation amount as per the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition and Rehabilitation and Settlement Act, 2013 for the land situated at Mauza - Kahudag,
Thana No. 288, old Khata No. 105, New Khata No. 256 Khesra No.
240,772,771,326,242 P.S- Barachatti, Anchal-Barachatti, District- Gaya area as per acquired which has been acquired Patna High Court CWJC No.3376 of 2025(2) dt.04-03-2025 for the project of broadening of NH-02 Six Lane Road (Aurangabad-chordaha).

(ii) For issuance of an appropriate writ in the nature of Mandamus for commanding and directing the respondent authorities to fix and pay the compensation amount of the acquired land as per value of the commercial land as my hotel adjacent to NH-02 was running smoothly and in good condition.
Santosh Yadav vs The Chairman, on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56534221/

sentences.text: For issuance of an appropriate writ in the nature of Mandamus for commanding and directing the respondent authorities to pay the compensation amount as per present market value of the acquired land.

(iv) For issuance of any other appropriate writ/writs, order/orders, direction/directions for which the writ petitioner will be found entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that a notice in L.A. Case No. 94/2013-14 was issued to the petitioner on 09.11.2020, and the price for the construction of the house has been paid to him;
however, the price for the land has not been paid.
4. Learned counsel for the State submits that Annexure-5 is the letter No. 823 dated 25.04.2024 issued by the Patna High Court CWJC No.3376 of 2025(2) dt.04-03-2025 District Land Acquisition Officer, Gaya, to the Project Director, NH-02, Aurangabad, assuring payment to the petitioner for the land.
5. Learned counsel for the National Highway Authority of India submits that the letter issued by the Project Director, bearing letter No. 1298 dated 03.12.2024, to the Competent Authority-cum-District Land Acquisition Officer, Gaya, Bihar, intimates that a notification under Section 3A for Plot Nos. 240, 772, 771, 326, and 242 was published on 27.02.2013, but publication under Section 3D for the said plots has not yet been made.

6. It is made clear that Section 3D of the National Highways Act is a declaration of acquisition, and it is the stand of the Project Director that the declaration of acquisition for the land has not been made, then payment could not be made at this juncture.

7. In response, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the stand of the Project Director is incorrect, as the National Highway Authority of India has already taken possession of the said land from the petitioner.

8. In light of the contradictory stands -- on the one hand, the declaration of acquisition has not been made, while on Patna High Court CWJC No.3376 of 2025(2) dt.04-03-2025 the other, a decision has been taken by the respondent authorities -- further clarification is required.
9. In the circumstances, respondent authorities are directed to file counter affidavit in this matter.
10. As such, list this matter on 15.04.2025.

(Dr. Anshuman, J) Ashwini/-
U Santosh Yadav vs The Chairman, on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56534221/
